title: optimize-evals-1on1-prep-notes-2026-02-28
content:
Meeting: Optimize / Evals review (1:1 prep)
Date: 2026-03-04 (sync with Aisha)
Context: quick prep notes for my 1:1 with Aisha to walk through the recent eval run, discuss the small but consistent regression on the FAQ prompt set, and agree next steps for A/Bing the new prompt normalization.

Top-level goals for meeting:
- surface the regression impact (user-visible regression vs metric drift)
- decide whether to pause rollout for canary or continue with mitigations
- assign owners for root-cause investigation and follow-ups
- set timeline for re-eval and gating criteria for rollback

What I'll bring / show:
- eval-summary.csv (per-prompt metrics: BLEU/ROUGE-like score, accuracy, top-k recall) - 3 latest runs (baseline, +prompt-norm, +quant-tweak)
- sample failure cases (10 examples) grouped by error type (hallucination, truncated answer, formatting mismatch)
- A/B results: traffic split 10/90, early CTR/engagement proxy numbers (coarse)
- PR diff for prompt normalization (optimize/prompt-normalize) and short note on implementation assumptions

Key findings to highlight:
- Regression is concentrated on FAQ prompt set (long, template-like prompts with lots of bullet lists).
- Failure mode: answers drop in completeness (missing bullet items) and occasional hallucinated list items.
- Metric delta: mean answer-completeness score down 6.2% vs baseline; other prompt sets unchanged within noise.
- Canary A/B shows small lift in latency ( +8ms ) but not at SLA risk. Cost impact negligible.

Hypotheses (quick):
- Prompt normalization removed protective context markers that guided list-completion behavior.
- KV-cache/prefix handling with the new tokenizer path truncates certain list metadata for long prompts.
- Quantization tweak interacts with attention stability for long sequences (less likely but possible).

Questions for Aisha / agenda items:
1) Do we want to pause the canary and roll back to baseline while we triage? (pros/cons)
2) If we don't pause, what mitigation guardrails should we add (e.g., prefix-escape rules, lower rollout %)?
3) Priority of triage: should infra/serving-engineer (Casey) look at KV-cache traces first, or should we expand eval prompt set coverage to catch other subtle regressions?
4) What gating metrics do we require before re-deploy? (e.g., completeness delta < 2% on FAQ set + no new failures in smoke set)

Proposed next steps (draft):
- ACTION: pause rollout to 5% (from 10%) and enable extra logging for requests hitting FAQ prompt set - owner: Jamie - deadline: 2026-03-05 EOD
- ACTION: Casey to pull KV-cache traces and verify prefix retention for long prompts; estimate by 2026-03-06
- ACTION: Aisha to run expanded eval with augmented prompt variations (add 25 edge-case prompts) and share results by 2026-03-06
- ACTION: Create quick revert PR (automated) and a checklist for rollback if completeness delta > 4% after next run - owner: Jamie - draft by 2026-03-06
- ACTION: Product to notify 2 customers in pilot if we detect user-visible regressions (Aisha) - done-by 2026-03-07 if triggered

Risks / notes:
- If we roll back, we might lose some latency improvements from prompt-norm but preserve user experience. Need to quantify net unit-cost change.
- Logging on production for FAQ set could increase token egress for debug; cap sample rate to 1% initially.

Data to attach in meeting:
- links: CONFLUENCE-OPT-457 (eval run notes), JIRA-OPT-1298 (regression ticket), https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/89 (prompt norm PR)
- csvs: eval-summary.csv, sample-failures.csv, ab-traffic-summary.csv

Prep checklist (done / todo):
- [x] collect latest eval runs (baseline, new1, new2)
- [x] select 10 representative failure examples
- [x] reproduce on local model (small) to sanity-check error is not infra-only
- [ ] instrument selective logging for FAQ prompt set in canary
- [ ] confirm rollback automation ready with on-call (SRE)

Notes for 1:1 flow:
- 5m quick context and TL;DR
- 10m walk through eval metrics + show 3 sample failures
- 10m discuss hypotheses and triage plan (Casey involvement)
- 5m agree on actions + owners + deadlines

Open thoughts / later follow-ups:
- Consider adding a lightweight prompt property metadata (e.g., "list-style: numbered|bulleted|qa") into eval harness to quickly slice results by expected output shape.
- Explore small synthetic tests for list-completion behavior that can run in CI as a smoke test (cheap).

End of notes.
